meta.title: Middle Eastern politics knowledge network, c. 1950-2026
meta.description: Key works and debates in Middle Eastern politics: authoritarian resilience and the coercive apparatus, monarchies and ruling bargains, rentier states and oil, elections and clientelism under authoritarianism, the Arab uprisings and their aftermath, Islamist movements and the inclusion-moderation debate, religion and politics, civil-military relations and coups, sectarianism and identity, civil wars and intervention, the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, Iran, Turkey and democratic backsliding, state formation and colonial legacies, Arab public opinion, gender, migration and refugees, great powers and regional order, and crony capitalism and economic reform. Works shared with the other maps are imported from them; others are top-cited 2006-2026 articles selected via Crossref (Middle East studies and political science journals) and anchoring books and classics. Direction: source (later or dependent work) -> target (earlier or anchoring work).

edge_types.builds_on: source extends or relies on target's argument or evidence
edge_types.challenges: source contests target's claim, mechanism or evidence
edge_types.qualifies: source adds a scope condition or moderating factor to target
edge_types.extends_to_new_case: source applies target's logic to a new population, period or domain
edge_types.synthesizes: source integrates target with other work
edge_types.mechanism_tested_by: source tests a mechanism implied by target

meta.verification: Repo works come from the user's Zotero library. Works imported from the other maps keep their verification. Crossref-selected works take title, authors, year, venue and DOI from Crossref records. Anchors are checked in Crossref separately; see each node's `verified` field. One-line claims for non-repo works are my summaries.
